## What I do

I'm a scientist who turns complex technical problems into clear decisions, combining AI/ML-driven image analysis and quantitative modelling with the ability to align specialists across teams.

During my PhD at [IST Austria](https://ista.ac.at/en/home/) in the [Heisenberg](https://heisenberglab.pages.ist.ac.at/) and [Hannezo](https://hannezo.pages.ist.ac.at/) labs, I built image-analysis and modelling pipelines to decode noisy live-imaging data, revealing how cells' internal skeletons coordinate movement across whole embryonic tissues. The work was published in [Nature Communications](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-72366-z), helped secure **€500K+ in research funding**, and along the way I trained **10+ early-career researchers** in microscopy and data analysis.

After my PhD, I spent a year as ISTA's **Image Analysis Expert**, advising **500+ researchers** on experimental design and analytical pipelines and helping them turn technical roadblocks into practical next steps. I also led the migration of **60+ microscopy workstations** across imaging, IT, and cybersecurity teams with zero disruption to operations, which was a reminder that even deeply technical work succeeds or fails on communication, trust, and attention to what people actually need.

Outside the lab, I led the social-media team at [PhD Balance](https://www.phdbalance.com/), a global NGO, growing its community to **25,000 followers over five years**. I also co-founded two international academic seminar series that ran **100+ sessions across four years**—both built through shared enthusiasm rather than formal authority or dedicated resources.

I&rsquo;m now looking for roles in deep-tech startups and life-science consulting, where I can help teams move from messy data and uncertainty to clear next steps. [Let&rsquo;s talk](https://www.linkedin.com/in/suyash-naik-s167s/).

### [6 Hours to Fully Reproduce 5 Years of Research — The Efficiency System Behind It](projects/efficiency-pipeline.qmd)
How I built an end-to-end analysis pipeline that condensed 40 TB of PhD data into 12 fully reproducible figures. The real stress-test: the day before my defence, I wanted a new colour scheme for my slides — so I regenerated every figure in the paper in a single afternoon. The system held.
